item.title: Patient was topless while isolated in Roscommon's psychiatric unit for nearly 24 hours - watchdog
item.description: A patient was topless while isolated in Roscommon's psychiatric unit for nearly 24 hours. The mental health watchdog has raised serious concern about this in a new report. This morning, the Mental Health Commission published its annual inspection report into the Department of Psychiatry in Roscommon University Hospital. item.title: Work to begin shortly on major housing development in Monksland
item.description: Construction work is expected to start next month on a large social housing development, with over 50 homes, in south Roscommon. Roscommon County Council has also given an update on other housing projects. The planning go-ahead was given last year for 51 homes at Sli an Choiste in Monksland. Advertisement Roscommon County Council says the tender assessment is now complete. Work is due to get under way by the end of next month. item.title: New maternity outpatient facility opens at Portiuncula
item.description: The opening of a new outpatient facility at Portiuncula University Hospital is a step in the right direction for maternity services there. That's according to local councillor Alan Harney who says the new service is a positive development for the hospital. The new outpatient facility was officially opened yesterday at the Ballinasloe hospital. item.title: Planning talks begin for controversial wind farm in Ballaghaderreen
item.description: Controversial plans for 10 wind turbines in Ballaghaderreen are set to be lodged with An Coimisiún Pleanála. The developer is already in talks with the planning body. Renewable energy firm Statkraft is planning this wind farm for several townlands just northwest of Ballaghaderreen, close to the Mayo border. item.title: Man hospitalised following alleged assault in Athlone
item.description: A man has been hospitalised following an alleged assault in Athlone yesterday afternoon. Gardaí say they attended the scene at around 3.30pm. A man in his 30's was brought to Portiuncula University Hospital for treatment of serious injuries. Investigations are ongoing. Advertisement

item.title: Seanad hears calls for Farming Rathcroghan Project to remain open
item.description: The Seanad has heard the need for the Farming Rathcroghan Project to remain open. In late January, the award-winning initiative, which has supported 90 farmers in managing more than 260 archaeological sites over the past eight years announced it was to cease operations. Despite repeated efforts, the project says state agencies responsible for heritage have provided little financial backing.
